title: Magnitude 3.0 Earthquake Hits Istmina at Dawn
seoTitle: Magnitude 3.0 Earthquake Hits Istmina at Dawn
subtitle: Colombian Geological Survey recorded the shallow earthquake on August 22, 2026.
excerpt: A magnitude 3.0 earthquake shook the municipality of Istmina early on August 22, 2026. Learn how to report it and what precautions to take.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A magnitude 3.0 earthquake was recorded in the early hours of Saturday, August 22, 2026, in the municipality of Istmina, located in the department of Chocó. The seismic event had a shallow depth, according to data released by the Colombian Geological Survey.

Tremor Details and Official Response

The seismic movement occurred at 5:32 a.m. on August 22, 2026. The entity responsible for monitoring seismic activity in the country indicated that the epicenter was located in Istmina.

How to Report the Felt Tremor

The Colombian Geological Survey maintains official channels available to gather information from people who felt the event. Citizens who perceived the shaking can submit a report through the platforms enabled by the institution.

Setting Up Alerts on Compatible Phones

Compatible phones have options to receive earthquake warnings. To check this feature, the user can access device settings, select the option corresponding to safety and emergency, and subsequently look for the earthquake alerts section. If this alternative does not appear, it is possible to access the location section, enter advanced options, and check the availability of the tool.

Sensor System Operation

The system is based on information obtained through sensors to identify seismic movements. With this data, the mechanism is able to estimate essential characteristics, such as the exact location and magnitude of the event.

Prevention and Safety Guidelines

The entity advises families to maintain an emergency preparedness plan. Among the main recommended preventive measures are the following:

  • Establish a clear evacuation route
  • Identify safe locations inside and outside spaces
  • Prepare a kit with water, a flashlight, a radio, non-perishable food, and identification documents

During the movement, the primary instruction is to stay calm and seek shelter in safe zones, staying away from windows and objects that could fall. After it ends, it is essential to act with caution, avoid using elevators, and not run or push other people. It is also recommended to check for possible structural damage to buildings before returning and to shut off gas, water, and power supplies if there is an imminent risk.

With information from El Tiempo.
